lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Where are all the beautiful people, Hermes — the men and the women? I'm new. Give me the tour.
lines.note: Menippus as eager tourist, completely unbothered by his surroundings.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: I don't have time for sightseeing, Menippus. But — look over there. To the right. That's Hyacinthus. Narcissus. Nireus. Achilles. Tyro. Helen. Leda. All the great beauties of antiquity, more or less.
lines.note: Hermes rattles off the names like a distracted docent pointing at exhibits he's described ten thousand times.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: All I see is bones. Skulls with no flesh on them. Most of them look the same.
lines.note: Flat. Genuinely puzzled. Not trying to make a point — yet.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: Yes, well. Those are the very bones every poet in history has been rhapsodising about. You seem underwhelmed.
lines.note: Dry. Hermes has clocked the joke but won't dignify it.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Show me Helen specifically. I wouldn't be able to pick her out on my own.
lines.note: Deadpan. The request is sincere, which makes it funnier.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: This skull here. This is Helen.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: And for this [pause] a thousand ships were fitted out from every corner of Greece. Greeks and barbarians died by the thousands. Cities were wiped off the map.
lines.note: Not rhetorical outrage — genuine arithmetic puzzlement, as though working out a sum that doesn't add up.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: You never saw her alive, Menippus. If you had, you'd have said yourself it was entirely reasonable to suffer so much, so long, for a woman like that. Flowers look shapeless when they're dry and the colour's gone — obviously. But when they're in bloom, they're beautiful. That's the whole point.
lines.note: Hermes is making a genuine philosophical argument, which is slightly out of character and he knows it.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: So what I find remarkable, Hermes, is that the Greeks couldn't see they were going to all that trouble for something that fades so fast and so easily.
lines.note: Still not moralising — just observing. The observation lands like a punchline because he's right and there's nothing more to say.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: I really don't have time to do philosophy with you. Pick a spot — wherever you like — lie down, make yourself at home. I have the rest of the dead to collect.
lines.note: Hermes exits mid-conversation, which is the only response available to him. The comedy is that Menippus has won by simply asking questions.
